stated: The Conservative Party will prevent new waste incinerators from being built, including those with recent permit approvals where substantial construction has not taken place, recognising the impact on local communities and increased recycling rates.

source.quote: We will prevent new waste incinerators being built, including those with recent permit approvals, revoking those where substantial construction has not taken place. This recognises the impact on local communities and that increased recycling rates will reduce the need for incineration capacity in the longer term.

bearing_set.reason: Preventing new incinerators directly affects local air quality (particulate, dioxin, NOx emissions) and the emissions trajectory of waste management, while the stated rationale of promoting recycling rates also bears on the broader environmental pathway — all core O6 indicators.

Blocking new incineration capacity constrains future waste-disposal options for local authorities; alternatives (landfill subject to escalating landfill-tax, waste export, new recycling infrastructure) carry higher per-tonne costs, creating a concrete pressure on council budgets and public finances over the medium term.

membership_note: O6 is the primary bearing (air quality, emissions, recycling-vs-burning counterfactual). O12 earns a secondary bearing via a specific fiscal mechanism: incinerators are a cost-efficient disposal route for residual waste, and blocking new capacity forces local authorities toward more expensive alternatives, materially affecting the funded/unfunded balance of waste management budgets. Community health/wellbeing concerns cited in the policy text route to O6 (environment) rather than O15, as the mechanism is environmental quality rather than social trust or cohesion. O13 effects (electricity generation from EfW) are too small and indirect relative to total generation to clear the non-negligible bar.
